claims.supported_statement: An inpatient conversational-EEG pilot involved 13 patients; replayed detector fine-tuning using patient push-button labels reduced false alarms in the study.
locators: Discussion: Limitations of our results; Ethical considerations; Methods: Platform implementation.
claims.evidence_scope: Single-site feasibility with offline pseudoprospective detector evaluation; no clinical benefit claim.
limitations: Small selected inpatient cohort in a supervised, artificial setting.
Detector improvements were replayed offline, not a live randomized adaptive-care trial.
Sensitivity did not improve; remaining false alarms may still burden patients.

verification.supported_scope: Single-site feasibility with offline pseudoprospective detector evaluation; no clinical benefit claim.
verification.reason: Rechecked extracted full primary methods/results/limitations and source status before drafting; material claims use the stated locators.

study.design: Prospective interface use, followed by offline pseudoprospective rolling detector fine-tuning.
study.setting: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania epilepsy monitoring unit.
study.population_or_dataset: 13 patients undergoing scalp (11) or intracranial (2) video-EEG monitoring.

sample_sizes.unit: patients in pilot and push-button replay analysis
sample_sizes.reason: Not 13 independent hospitals or randomized arms.
Distinct analysis; its effect must not be substituted for the 13-patient push-button result.

study.comparator: Baseline detector versus sequentially fine-tuned detector on future unseen segments in offline replay.
primary_endpoints: Seizure-detector false alarms per hour, sensitivity and F1 in replay; interface feasibility.
secondary_exploratory_endpoints: Patient engagement; separate app-response and clinician-label simulations.

results.units: relative percent and false alarms per hour
results.uncertainty: Small selected cohort; simulation, not live treatment efficacy.
results.locator: Results: Patient-in-the-loop model fine-tuning; Figure 5b, middle panel.

study.follow_up: Short inpatient EMU stays; no long-term outpatient clinical follow-up established.
study.harms: No powered adverse-event or patient-benefit trial; daily review of AI interactions was a study safeguard.
study.analysis_notes: Do not conflate the 77.8% per-model comparison with the separate full-stay replay estimate. LLM delivered information; seizure detector, not the LLM, was fine-tuned.
study.applicability: Feasibility of patient/device interaction and a detector adaptation strategy; does not establish safe autonomous care or outpatient patient benefit.
